sections.h2: Which Vermilion County office answers which tax question?
sections.html:
Vermilion County divides property tax questions among four offices in Danville, and the Treasurer's page names each one. Calling the right one first saves a transfer.

  • County Clerk, 217-554-1903: tax rates, tax codes and delinquent property tax information.
  • Recorder, 217-554-6040: deed information.
  • Supervisor of Assessments, 217-554-1940: name and address changes, assessed values and exemptions.
  • Treasurer, 217-554-6080: tax bill and payment information.

The Treasurer's counter opens at 8:00 a.m. and closes at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays that are not legal holidays. The Supervisor of Assessments sits on the third floor of the Joseph G. Cannon Building at 201 North Vermilion Street, where the Board of Review also takes filings.

sections.h2: What makes Vermilion County different for a home seller?
sections.html:
Vermilion County runs along the Indiana line between the state border and Champaign County. It was incorporated on January 18, 1826, as the 45th of Illinois' 102 counties, and at 901 square miles it ranks as the seventh largest. Danville is both the county seat and its biggest city. The county's name comes from the Vermilion River, and Lake Vermilion, a 1,000-acre reservoir northwest of Danville, supplies the city's water.

The population was 74,188 in 2020 and is estimated at 71,259 for 2025. Of 34,407 housing units, 11.2 percent stand vacant, and owners occupy 67.8 percent of the homes that are lived in. Danville Area Community College is in the county.

Interstate 74 passes along Danville's southern edge, with U.S. 136, U.S. 150 and Illinois Route 1 meeting downtown. Four rail lines cross the Danville area, so crossings near a house can matter to a buyer. Abraham Lincoln practiced law in Danville from 1841 to 1859, and the Fithian home, where he once spoke, is now the Vermilion County Museum. Twelve school districts serve the county.

sections.h2: What were the Vermilion County 2026 tax payment dates?
sections.html:
Thursday, June 18, 2026 was the first installment date. Friday, September 4 was the second, and also the date for mobile home taxes. The Treasurer then listed a run of cutoffs ahead of the sale.

Vermilion County Treasurer payment calendar for 2026

Checks are made payable to Vermilion County Treasurer, and the phone payment line is 1 (877) 221-8591. Owners who want electronic bills can register at vermilion.mcgedoc.com using the code printed on their current statement.

sections.h2: How does a Vermilion County owner contest an assessment?
sections.html:
A complaint about a 2026 assessment is due at the Board of Review 30 calendar days after the township assessor and Supervisor of Assessments publish their changes, tracking 35 ILCS 200/16-55. The board's 2026 rules supply the practical steps.

  • File on the board's approved form, in duplicate, with a complete copy of every document you want considered.
  • Use a separate form for each tract number. The form covers residential, commercial and industrial property, and farmland has its own form.
  • File in person, email brdreview@vercounty.org, or mail it to 201 North Vermilion St, 3rd Floor, Danville, IL 61832.
  • Ownership on January 1 of the assessment year is required.

A complaint filed in 2026 touches only the 2026 assessment, which drives the bill payable in 2027. The bill that arrives in 2026 rests on the 2025 assessment. Tax rates are outside the board's power, and it will not hear complaints about them.

sections.h2: What happens after a Vermilion County complaint is filed?
sections.html:
The board reviews the complaint and the attached papers, may look at the property, and mails a Notice of Proposed Decision. An owner who disagrees must request a hearing in writing, on the board's form, within 10 days of the notice date.

A hearing notice follows at least 10 days ahead of the date, and a no-show means dismissal. The board recommends an attorney when the reduction sought is $100,000 or more on a parcel or a combination of parcels.

The board's rules also address appraisals. Any appraisal must meet the Real Estate Appraiser Licensing Act and USPAP, state whether the appraiser is licensed in Illinois, and list the board and Vermilion County as intended users when it supports a complaint. The board will not issue a certificate of error for a mere error of judgment in valuation. After the board rules, a petition to the state Property Tax Appeal Board is possible within 30 days of the written decision notice (35 ILCS 200/16-160).

sections.h2: How does the Supervisor of Assessments organize Vermilion County values?
sections.html:
The Supervisor of Assessments office was created by state law to give statistical and performance data to the Illinois Department of Revenue and technical advice to the township assessors and the Board of Review. It keeps the name and address records, assessed values and exemptions, equalizes assessments, and acts as clerk of the Board of Review. It publishes the assessment change notices and mails them to taxpayers.

Vermilion County posts a 2023 quadrennial assessment roll, payable in 2024, for 19 townships: Blount, Butler, Carroll, Catlin, Danville, Elwood, Georgetown, Grant, Jamaica, Love, McKendree, Middlefork, Newell, Oakwood, Pilot, Ross, Sidell, South Ross and Vance. A parcel's township determines which assessor owns the first look at its value.

sections.h2: What tax relief does Vermilion County point owners to?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's relief page lists two programs. The first is the Senior Citizens and Disabled Persons Property Tax Relief and Pharmaceutical Assistance Act, with applications from the Illinois Department of Revenue at 800-624-2459. The second is the Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program, and its applications are available in the Treasurer's office at 217-554-6080.

Exemptions that lower the assessed value, such as the homestead exemptions, go through the Supervisor of Assessments instead. The county also posts an application for a general homestead exemption on single-family dwellings subject to a lease.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Vermilion County taxes?
sections.html:
An installment unpaid after its due date is delinquent and accrues interest of 1 1/2 percent a month or part of one, the rate 35 ILCS 200/21-15 sets for counties below 3,000,000 people. Later in the fall the county publishes names of unpaid owners and holds a sale of the taxes, in 2026 on November 4.

Whoever buys at the sale gets a tax lien, and the owner keeps a right to redeem. For certificates issued from 2024 forward, 35 ILCS 200/21-350 allows 3 years after the sale, with exceptions. Delinquent-tax questions go to the County Clerk at 217-554-1903, ideally before a closing.

A Vermilion County house with taxes owed can still go to a cash buyer as is, and the balance is cleared at closing.

faqs.q: When were Vermilion County property taxes due in 2026?
faqs.a: The first installment was due June 18, 2026, and the second installment and mobile home taxes were due September 4. The Treasurer stopped taking payments after November 3.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for a Vermilion County assessment complaint?
faqs.a: Thirty calendar days from publication of your township's assessment changes. File two copies on the board's form with supporting documents attached.

faqs.q: Can the Vermilion County board adjust my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. Rates are beyond the board's authority, and it turns away rate complaints. Only the assessed value of the property is reviewable.

faqs.q: Which Vermilion County office has delinquent tax records?
faqs.a: The County Clerk, at 217-554-1903. For bills and payments, the Treasurer's line is 217-554-6080.

faqs.q: Is there a deferral program for seniors in Vermilion County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer lists a Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program, and applications are available at that office. The Illinois Department of Revenue also supplies applications for the Senior Citizens and Disabled Persons relief act.
